hint: The interquartile range is the distance between the lower quartile and the upper quartile.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Sort the data from least to greatest first — many statistics get easy after that.
The interquartile range is the distance between the lower quartile and the upper quartile.
The quartiles are given as $Q1 = 7$ and $Q3 = 20$, so take the smaller away from the larger: $20 - 7$.
$20 - 7 = 13$, so the IQR of this data is $13$.

explanation: The quartiles check out: the lower half $5, 7, 9$ has median $7$ and the upper half $15, 20, 25$ has median $20$.
The IQR is the spread of the middle half, found as $Q3 - Q1$.
Subtract: $20 - 7 = 13$, so the IQR of this data is $13$.
